# Correctness verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES

PR #191 at `cafc9085aba3ef2c5ffddb6ce638471f467b33ba`, answering `01a1bc04-2469-7251-a6bd-8d8affa34af3`, against main `a244cb479eed70d4098e72d9d0b0a6f41d0ffda9`. No new correctness blocker.

**Admission:** `check_instance` uses the requested `render::is_name` grammar, and escapes/bounds the E-RS-ARG diagnostic (`crates/daemon/src/community/layout.rs:75-101`). Single assign calls `new_role_and_instance`; assign batch uses the same helper; both lineage forms pass through `past_holding` and that helper (`http/directory.rs:1198-1202,1278-1294,1323,1362,1462-1468,1505-1512`). All batch rows are parsed before the recording writer is called, so a malformed row cannot partially apply. Optional no-instance holdings remain supported.

**Legacy compatibility:** single and batch release retain the loose parser (`http/directory.rs:1201,1614`), with only escaped diagnostic text changed. Rebuild still reads holders documents and checks row invariants without applying the new admission grammar (`community/directory.rs:754-793`; `community/holders.rs:33-59`). No release/rebuild acceptance rule was tightened by this patch.

**Addresses/windows:** role-address instances now use the same name grammar before routing (`delivery/role_send.rs:76-83`). Every holding-derived window name renders project, role and instance (`community/directory.rs:2623-2631`). Both kept-window reasons are fixed text; release's seat-name fallback is rendered; the only rename sink receives those names (`:1621-1693`). CLI holdings receipts additionally check the complete window name through `render::window` (`crates/cli/src/main.rs:3127`; `crates/core/src/render.rs:81-94`). The kept-window regression tests the intended no-rename case, not a live tmux launch; actual rename sanitization is established by the shared formatter and its call sites.

**N001, inherited refusal over-claim:** `RoleAddress::parse` still interpolates the entire raw `to` in its refusal (`delivery/role_send.rs:80-83`), and `http/role_send.rs:260-279` puts that string in `meta`. This branch predates the PR, but the new API paragraph's claim that address refusals are escaped and bounded is inaccurate. The long-address test asserts only E-RS-ROLE-ADDRESS. The author confirmed this limitation. Escape/bound the rejected address and add a hostile-address diagnostic regression, or qualify the documentation; the recording-path E-RS-ARG refusals themselves are escaped/bounded as requested.

**Proof:** CI run `42500185891`, artifact `13625501056`, contains 2,265 passing Rust cases, zero failures/errors; nextest separately reports five skipped cases. The forged-key HTTP test, hostile kept-window test, CLI window line, grammar unit test and existing assign/lineage batch atomicity tests all executed. Rust lint, Node 22/24 checks and delivers passed; `pr-freeze` returned FINAL with matching remote/GitHub SHA and a clean detached worktree.

Inspected the author's retained V1-V6/X1-X3 index, mutation runner and original mutation-result events. The first V1 failed its three-match anchor assertion and ran an unmutated passing baseline; it is not a kill. Its unique-anchor rerun and V2-V6/X1-X3 each have an actual panic and FAILED test result. The runner restores each file; subsequent gate output reports success. Guard-source transfer from the reported `9036e10e` and window source committed as `106f36ef` was checked; the V killing test body is byte-identical at this head. These are author executions transferred across unchanged source, not reviewer-run mutants at cafc908.

**Cost/scope:** bounded in-process validation/rendering, with the existing at-most-one window rename per assignment/release and zero rename for a kept window. No new loop, poll, timer, hook, sweep or launch site; no live-rate claim. No local reviewer builds/tests, product edits, credential reads, merge, push or review-HEAD movement. Security and performance verdicts remain independently owned.
